clue.text: Dad on bass held back music of his youth?

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the first-named piece after what follows it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
rit., short for ritardando, is the musical direction meaning held back or slowing
pop is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A father with a bass guitar plays more slowly while revisiting the music he loved as a teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held back' looks like restraint, but it is the musical direction ritardando, abbreviated as on a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was the 1990s guitar-band genre, so it is the music a present-day dad grew up with; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Blast fellow switching sides during contest

indicators.note: during means within the contest, so the fellow goes inside

parts.note: a bee is a competition, as in a spelling bee
a rat is someone who deserts to the other side

explanation.surface: A fellow who changes sides mid-contest gets blasted.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast someone is to criticise them harshly, the same as berating them.

clue.text: Call on president, assuming envoy's content

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the president's name takes the other letters inside

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

indicators.note: content means what is inside, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: the word envoy, whose inside letters are used

explanation.surface: A diplomat's message calls on the president.
explanation.walkthrough: Ike was Dwight Eisenhower's nickname; 'content' takes only the inside of the envoy's word.
explanation.definitionFit: To invoke a power or authority is to appeal or call on it for help.

clue.text: Attractive means of getting a drink, more or less

parts.note: pretty means attractive
a well is a source of drinking water

explanation.surface: An attractive way to get a drink, roughly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means almost or nearly, an approximation.

clue.text: Official home for bishop wanting a post

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so one letter is left out

parts.note: a bishop's official residence is a palace

explanation.surface: A bishop's residence lacks a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or place is a position or job someone holds.

clue.text: Wild flower trail expanded

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail or follow them
rose means swelled or increased, as dough rises

explanation.surface: A wild flower spreads along a path, growing larger.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a common climbing wild rose of hedgerows.

clue.text: Old three-halfpenny comic incomplete, one part damaged

indicators.note: incomplete means the comic's title loses its last letter

parts.note: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of 'part' are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An old comic, worth three halfpence, is incomplete, with one part damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a British comic weekly; DAND plus I plus a rearranged PART gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandiprat was a small sixteenth-century English coin worth three halfpence, later a word for a puny person.

clue.text: One way of getting out as match proceeds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an opening in a fence or wall
second meaning: the money taken from spectators at a match

explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' reads as a verb, the match going on, but it is the noun meaning takings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an exit in a wall and the takings or attendance at a sporting fixture.

clue.text: Established novelist links up on air

indicators.note: on air means broadcast, so the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: a novelist is an author, and a spacecraft docks when it links up: author docks

explanation.surface: A writer joins a broadcast on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means conventional or accepted, as an established view or practice is.

clue.text: One outcome of simple test for sucker?

parts.note: easy means simple
a mark is one outcome of the test the clue mentions, a score

explanation.surface: A simple test results in someone being taken for a sucker.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, a mark is one outcome of a test, here a simple one: an easy mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy mark is a person readily cheated or fooled, a gullible victim.

clue.text: Auditor's assessment for variety show

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the auditor's version is the word as heard rather than written

parts.note: a review is a critical assessment

explanation.surface: An accountant's assessment of the books seems to be about a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditor looks like a financial checker, but here it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances, a mixed programme.

clue.text: Provides commentary for girl leading seaman round gallery

indicators.note: leading puts the girl's name in front of the rest

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: round means the seaman's letters go around the gallery

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A girl guides a sailor around an art gallery, explaining the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's well-known art gallery, and an ordinary seaman is abbreviated as in naval ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate is to add explanatory notes, a form of written commentary.

clue.text: Select a particular song and walk out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: take, that is choose, the air, a tune
second meaning: go outdoors for some fresh air

explanation.walkthrough: An air is a melody, so the phrase read literally means picking a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go outside for a stroll, while taken literally it means choosing a melody.

clue.text: Swallow or martin consuming other birds' food?

indicators.note: consuming means the words around it eat up the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: A swallow or a martin eats what other birds eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of Swallow, all of 'or' and the start of martin.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms are a staple prey of thrushes and blackbirds, though swallows and martins catch insects instead; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Troops look cross mounting guard at entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means the pieces climb, so they are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are troops
to peek is to look
a rood is a cross, as in a church's rood screen

explanation.surface: Soldiers, looking angry, take up guard duty at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like anger but is a crucifix; RE PEEK ROOD climbs to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorkeeper is a porter or attendant who controls who comes through a building's door.

clue.text: Artwork could make attendant blush, were I to go in

indicators.note: 'were I to go' means the letter I is to leave the attendant's word

parts.note: a waiter attends at table
to colour is to blush

explanation.surface: A painting might make an attendant blush, if I went in to view it.
explanation.walkthrough: Put I into the answer's first part and you get WAITER COLOUR, attendant blush; so take I from WAITER to leave WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A watercolour is a painting done in water-based paints, a kind of artwork.

clue.text: Against harsh assessment of some bedding

parts.note: to can mean against, as in 'back to the wall'
grating means harsh or jarring

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a harsh review of their bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: A tog rating is the British warmth scale printed on duvets.
explanation.definitionFit: Duvets are labelled with a tog value, a measure of how warm the quilt is.

clue.text: Not keen on horse trained overseas

parts.note: to be off something is to have lost one's liking for it

indicators.note: trained means shaped or drilled, so the letters of horse are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a horse trained abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshore means located abroad or out at sea, especially of money or companies.

clue.text: Blustery at first with more showers, becoming brighter

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of blustery is used

parts.note: rainier means having more rain

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: windy early on, more showers, then clearing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The weather surface makes 'brighter' look like sunshine; it means cleverer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighter here means more intelligent, the same as being cleverer.

clue.text: Combatant repressing rage left bar, starting ignition

indicators.note: repressing means holding something in, so the combatant's word contains the rest

parts.note: a fighter is a combatant
ire means rage

explanation.surface: A fighter holds back his rage and leaves the bar to start something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub to leave, but it is the shape of the fuel block.
explanation.definitionFit: A firelighter is a small block of flammable material used to get a fire going.

clue.text: Shock in city rising after treasurer cleared out

indicators.note: after places the city's word after the treasurer's letters
cleared out means emptied, leaving only its outside letters
in a down clue rising means read upwards, back to front

parts.note: Rome is a city

explanation.surface: A city is shaken after its treasurer runs off with the funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking, especially a small earthquake, so a shock.

clue.text: Asian primate rushes all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monkey rushes about everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey native to South and East Asia.

clue.text: Husband roped in to sample traditionally female craft

indicators.note: roped in means drawn into a group, so the husband's letter goes inside

parts.note: to sip is to taste or sample

explanation.surface: A husband is persuaded to try a craft traditionally done by women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female craft' suggests sewing or knitting, but it is a vessel, which sailors call 'she'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are customarily referred to as she, so a vessel is the female craft.

clue.text: Tracked down and slaughtered another rat

indicators.note: slaughtered means destroyed or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A hunter found one more rat and killed it.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something to earth, like a hunted fox to its burrow, is to find it after a long search.

clue.text: Penny-pinching firm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' could be a business, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stingy with money and held securely in place.

clue.text: Good time for delivery?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a very enjoyable time
second meaning: in cricket each delivery from the bowler is a ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Good time for delivery' suggests a baby due date; in cricket a delivery is one bowled ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a thoroughly enjoyable time and a single bowled delivery in cricket.

clue.text: Old team showing its age, getting rusty?

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team
something dating is becoming old-fashioned

explanation.surface: An old sports side is ageing and losing its sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting rusty' suggests losing skill, but it is literal rust.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust forms when iron combines with oxygen, so a metal turning rusty is undergoing oxidation.

clue.text: Little doggies carrying master's shoes

indicators.note: carrying means the puppies' word holds the other letter inside

parts.note: pups are young dogs
M is the abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: Puppies carry off their owner's shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumps are light flat shoes, such as court shoes or plimsolls.

clue.text: Screwed up large stopper to protect drum

indicators.note: screwed up means crumpled, so the following letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A big stopper is screwed into place to protect a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed up' reads as a phrase, but only 'Screwed' signals the rearrangement; 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is protected from loud noise by a plug pushed into the ear canal.

clue.text: Flipping annoyed on backing corrupt fighters in ring

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' puts the first piece after the second
backing means the word for corrupt goes into reverse

parts.note: to rot is to corrupt or decay

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word for annoyed is read backwards

parts.note: sore means annoyed

explanation.surface: Annoyed, dishonest fighters battle in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse, but it reverses SORE to EROS; ROT backed becomes TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Toreros are bullfighters, who fight in the bullring.
